name: Mountain climber
summary: From a high plank, drive one knee toward the chest, then switch legs fast.
setup: High plank, hands under the shoulders. Bring one knee toward the chest, return it, then the other, keeping the hips low and steady. Continue for the count.
why: The legs cross under the body too fast and too close together to count reliably. Logged by hand.
contraindications: Wrist or shoulder pain; back pain.

faults.label: Hips rising
faults.tip: Keep the body in a plank line; the knee comes to the chest under it.

faults.label: Bouncing the hips
faults.tip: The legs move; the trunk does not.

faults.label: Hands creeping back
faults.tip: As you tire the hands drift; reset them under the shoulders.

faults.label: Knees barely moving
faults.tip: Short, fast shuffles look busy but do nothing. Drive the knee forward.

guide.cannotSee: The legs — too fast and overlapping.

points.t: Plank line, hips low and still.
